podcast.title: Hidden CD Artwork Messages
podcast.body: The CD artwork for the "Box Car Racer" album contains hidden messages. For example, a sequence "LNW-1301" is the longitudinal location of the Twin Towers/World Trade Center. "If you have a copy of the CD, there are all kinds of hidden messages in the artwork."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

podcast.title: Name Origin
podcast.body: The name "Box Car Racer" was shared with a previous band Travis Barker was in before Blink 182. The common story that it alluded to the B-52 bomber that dropped the atomic bomb on Nagasaki is incorrect; its true origin is Travis's old band. "The real origin goes back to Travis's old band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

podcast.title: Origin and Purpose
podcast.body: Box Car Racer was Tom DeLonge's project, driven by his need to play more aggressive punk music and to occupy himself while recovering from back surgery. He did not envision it as a permanent band. "This was Tom's product and his chance to exercise his need to play punk that was dirtier and more aggressive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

podcast.title: Travis Barker's Involvement
podcast.body: Travis Barker joined Tom DeLonge on drums for Box Car Racer, a decision that deeply upset Mark Hoppus of Blink 182, who felt betrayed. Travis only sang on a couple of tracks. "But then he asked Travis to be his drummer, which was okay for Travis, but it greatly pissed off Mark."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Acoustic Style Comparison
xref.body: The early acoustic sound of Box Car Racer's concept album was compared to the kind of material produced by the Violent Femmes. "It started as an acoustic sort of record, not unlike the kind of stuff the violent fams did."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Mark Hoppus's Isolation During Side Projects
xref.body: While Tom DeLonge and Travis Barker pursued side projects like Box Car Racer and The Transplants, Mark Hoppus "stayed on the sidelines quietly fuming," feeling betrayed that Tom had asked Travis to drum for Box Car Racer, a project that had an "old DIY vibe of early Blink." "Mark left the studio and wrote what he thought would be an instant rejection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2
